reasoning: In this everyday adverb, ث is pronounced s. The final an is actually pronounced.
قبل has urban glottal ق, and interrogative ولا is walla. The suffix on بعدو refers back to eating or the meal.
This is the normal Arabic country name used in Palestinian conversation. The article remains il- before م.
The construct form of كلمة is kilmit, with an audible t. حق has a doubled glottal stop in urban speech.
This is a formal conjunction meaning while or whereas. Conversational temporal while can be expressed with وقت ما or a clause introduced by و.
جايزة means a prize or award without specifying its rank. Grand prize needs an additional qualifier such as الكبرى or الكبيرة.
The everyday Palestinian pronunciation has long ee, not the MSA diphthong ay.
This is the ordinary Ramallah word for where, with long ee.
This English borrowing is common in messaging contexts. The Arabicized pronunciation uses f, though speakers retaining the English pronunciation may use v.
This is the familiar idiom for accomplishing two things with one action. عصفورين has the colloquial dual ending een.
بتقبلو addresses multiple people, and ق is glottalized. كاش is the everyday borrowing for cash, while بس means only here.
The verb meaning improved is the past-tense form with doubled س. Palestinian speech reduces the initial syllable to t7-.
This is the ordinary past-tense he-form meaning pulled. It can also mean withdrew, depending on the object.
The past-tense verb has a reduced initial tw- cluster. Doubled ق becomes a doubled glottal stop in urban Ramallah speech.
The clothing reading is shurraab, distinct from sharaab meaning a drink. جراب and جرابات are also very common locally.
Colloquial nisir is commonly used for an eagle or similar large raptor. In precise zoological terminology, نسر denotes a vulture and عقاب an eagle.
This formula expresses hope that all is well or that nothing bad has happened. خير has Palestinian long ee.
بتعرف is the masculine singular present-tense form. The phrase naturally introduces something the speaker wants to say, like English you know what.
This is the past-tense he-form meaning volunteered. ط is emphatic and و is doubled.

meaning_fix: How are you, sweetheart / my dear? (to a man; not specifically Hebron)
reasoning: The parenthetical خليلي is a regional annotation, not part of the spoken greeting. The phrase itself is also natural in Ramallah, where قلبي is pronounced 'albi.
This conventional blessing wishes someone health or strength, often acknowledging their work. The verb has no b- prefix because it expresses a wish.
Everyday pronunciation commonly shortens the initial vowel to ijaar, although a fuller iijaar also occurs. It means rent or a rental payment.
The normal country name is بولندا, pronounced boolanda. بلاندا appears misspelled, so the literal blaanda reading is tentative.
This everyday loanword refers to a pajama outfit. The feminine ending after م is pronounced e.
As a noun, شارب means a mustache; the plural شوارب is also common. The noun label distinguishes it from the identically shaped participle meaning having drunk.
